title: Backing Into People
hook: Angled stall. The street behind you has people.
scene: Heavy rain under flat gray overcast in a downtown lot that still paints its stalls on a bias. You are nose-in, plow to the wall. Backing out puts you into a two-lane street. Two figures are already in that street — dark coats, not a crosswalk, walking the lane like it is a sidewalk. The lot wants you out. The street does not owe you a hole. You have to leave a stall into people who are not looking at a reverse lamp.
decision: You are nose-in and the street behind the stall has people. How do you leave?

options.text: Reverse now — they will see the lamps and move
options.result: You come out on a guess. They do not see the lamps in the rain. The plow is the wrong end for this. You write two coats into a stall exit. The lot did not need that sound.

options.text: Honk the whole reverse so they know a car is coming
options.result: You back up shouting. They jump and scatter into the other lane. A primer car has to lift. Sound got them off your paint and onto someone else's.

options.text: Wait until they pass, then creep out and stop if anyone new enters the street
options.result: You wait once and then commit. A third coat steps off the curb after you are already rolling. Waiting is not the same as checking the whole time you move.

options.text: Wait them out, check both ways, creep, and be ready to plant it the whole reverse
options.result: You let the coats clear. You look both ways. You creep. A third person appears and you plant it. They pass. You finish into an empty street. The stall stays a stall.

debrief: Angled and straight-in stalls back into a live street. People in that street own it until they are gone. Wait for them to clear, then creep.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: When backing out of angled or perpendicular parking, yield to people and traffic in the street; creep and be ready to stop.
